line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Bc5 Bc4 d6 Nxe5 dxe5 d3
teaches: A piece down, the temptation is to hunt the refutation right now — but there usually isn't one yet. The moves that make a sacrifice work are the boring ones, because the compensation is TIME, and time is only worth something once the pieces that spend it are out.
explains: You're a piece down and you want the knockout immediately — but it isn't there yet. The modest pawn to d3 holds the pawn on e4, opens the diagonal for the last minor piece, and the bishop on c4 is already safe. Nothing is threatened and nothing needs to be: you make the position solid before you make it sharp, because the compensation is time and time only pays once your pieces are on the board.

line: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3 Bc5 Bc4 d6 Nxe5 dxe5 d3 Qf6 O-O
teaches: An opponent who throws the queen out early to threaten mate is doing your work for you when you are behind on material — castle, and the same move that reaches safety also brings a rook to the defence and forces the queen to retreat.
explains: When you're behind on material, an opponent who throws the queen out early to threaten mate is doing your work for you. Castle: the king reaches safety, the rook lands on f1 defending the f2-square the queen was eyeing, and the queen that came out to threaten now has to spend a move retreating. Answer an early queen with development, never with panic.
